tasks.task: Check a workbook before it is shared or relied on

items.when: When a workbook is about to be shared, to map inputs and workings and hunt wrong ranges and hard-coded numbers
When you want a guided pass that ends in an issue list and the key figures re-worked
When the file is large, to list formula errors, broken links and totals that do not tie
When there is an old and a revised version, to see every changed value, formula and name
When the review finds buried assumptions, to log each one with its risk for the owner
When a total looks right, to re-work it a second way before you trust it

tasks.task: Write a formula with a worked example

items.when: When the client knows what to calculate but not the formula, or theirs is too long to follow
When the client must understand the formula, to show the smallest example with values traced
After the formula is filled down, to catch cells where the range or reference slipped

tasks.task: Fix a formula that errors or gives the wrong answer

items.when: When a cell shows an error code or a number the client knows is wrong
When one broken formula suggests the same fault sits elsewhere in the workbook
When the formula is right and the data is the cause: text numbers, blanks or odd dates

tasks.task: Build a quote or price calculator

items.when: When a business needs a new calculator built, tested and handed over in order
When the price list lives in the owner's head and must become inputs, rates and outputs cell by cell
When the request is one line, to ask the few questions that fix inputs, rates and outputs
When staff will type the job details, to give them dropdowns, clear entry cells and checks
When the calculator gives a price, to test it covers costs and what a discount does
When the calculator's result must go out as a branded quote in the client's template
Before handover, to test the calculator with edge cases and look for hard-coded numbers

tasks.task: Build a day-rate or job-cost sheet

items.when: When the owner wants to change one input and see the rate or job cost update
Before the sheet, to work out the hourly and day rate from target pay, costs and billable hours
When the job has stages, to cost each step and see which lines drain the margin
When materials are imported, to bring freight and duty into the cost per unit
When the sheet is built, to check profit per job by hand against the sheet's answer

tasks.task: Build a what-if model with three cases

items.when: When the owner needs low, base and high cases driven from one inputs block
When the model is about cash, to lay out 30, 60 and 90 days from invoices, bills and fixed costs
When each case rests on guesses, to log them so a reader sees what could change the answer
When the low case feels too kind, to test how bad one year can get before the business stops earning
When the model is drafted, to have figures re-worked and the assumption that matters most named

tasks.task: Build a budget or budget-against-actual sheet

items.when: When past numbers and plans must become a budget and a forecast with gaps noted
When the budget is split by team and phased by month
When spend should be read against budget every month, with reasons
Before the budget is shared, to check totals tie across tabs and nothing is counted twice

tasks.task: Design a tracker or log that other people fill in

items.when: When a new tracker must be built so others can use it safely
When the field list is agreed, to get a formatted empty file with no invented rows
When entries must be limited to allowed values with dropdowns and checks
When the owner is unsure what to track, to get a one-page sheet of seven numbers to react to
When the tracker goes to a new keeper, to check it against the field rules and write the guide
When the tracker uses the builder's words and not the words of the people who fill it in

tasks.task: Write an Excel macro for one repeat task

items.when: When a weekly chore should run from a button, with a plain plan, settings at the top and a backup step
Before any code, to write the manual steps exactly so the macro does the same job
When the macro is written, to list the cases to run on a copy: empty, one row, large and odd data
When the code is drafted, to catch repeated logic and common slips before the client runs it
When the macro tries to do everything at once and should grow in small tested steps

tasks.task: Clean up a recorded macro so it works on any data size

items.when: When a recorded macro worked once and now skips rows, errors or takes forever
When the recording is long, to plan small safe changes that do not alter what it does
When nobody knows what the macro should produce, to pin its output before you change it

tasks.task: Fix a macro or script that errors or runs slow

items.when: When a macro or script fails and the fix must stay safe for the people who press the button
When there is an error message or log, to find the cause and a fix that works
When the script was left half-working, to get clearer names and tidier error handling

tasks.task: Write a Google Apps Script for a repeat Sheets task

items.when: When a daily or weekly Sheets job should run on a timer or a button
When the script will be run by non-experts and needs settings on top and a safe test run
When the task starts from form replies that must be logged or sent as alerts
Before the client turns the timer on, to catch slips in the drafted script

tasks.task: Set up a Google Form to Sheet workflow

items.when: When each form reply should trigger an email, a log row or a sorted tab
When replies need a summary tab or reminders the form cannot do by itself
When a script may be the wrong tool, to compare a Zapier or Make setup
Before the team relies on it, to find double runs and what happens when a step fails
When replies must reach another app, to check what can be triggered and written

tasks.task: Build a scheduled report from a sheet

items.when: When a report is made by hand every week in Google Sheets and should send itself
When the client describes the report in plain words and wants a workbook they can rerun
When dated records must become a monthly summary with counts and totals you can trace
When the weekly report also needs a trend, a forecast and a dashboard to share
When report numbers are pasted into slides, to check each slide figure agrees with the workbook

tasks.task: Clean a messy sheet or export

items.when: When a sheet has stray spaces, text numbers, mixed dates and duplicates
When the same messy file arrives every month and the rules should be saved
When cleaning must keep the formulas and formatting intact
After cleaning, to count what gaps, duplicates and odd values remain

tasks.task: Match two lists and explain what does not match

items.when: When two tables share a key, to join them and explain unmatched rows and duplicate keys
When the client wants the lookup formula itself, with a worked example
When the two lists are a ledger and a bank statement, to sort the gaps by type

tasks.task: Build a summary tab, PivotTable or chart

items.when: Before the summary, to set who reads it, what they decide and the few numbers that fit
When raw rows must roll up by month with traceable totals and rates
When one clean chart with the right chart type is needed from the data
When the workbook has PivotTables, to set the refresh order and find stale outputs
When a chart is drafted, to check the chart type and axes do not mislead

tasks.task: Make a sheet safe for non-experts to use

items.when: When others will type into the sheet, to find where one wrong entry breaks the result
When free typing causes errors, to add an input form with allowed values and checks
When the sheet is correct but a new user cannot tell where to type or what happened

tasks.task: Write handover notes for a workbook or macro

items.when: When someone is taking over a workbook and must run it without calling you
When the next owner needs inputs, formulas, update steps and risks in one guide
When the handover includes a macro or script, to explain each part beside its reason
When the weekly routine needs exact steps, what to do if it fails and how to roll back

tasks.task: Run the quarterly spreadsheet health check

items.when: Every three months for the workbooks the business depends on, and before year end
When each workbook on the list needs its inputs, workings and outputs checked
When you have last quarter's copy, to see what changed since
When reports are built on PivotTables that may be stale

tasks.task: Set up a sheet to print or export cleanly

items.when: When a sheet prints across odd pages, to fix columns, repeated headers and page breaks
When the export feeds a slide deck, to check every figure still matches the workbook

tasks.task: Plan the move when a sheet has outgrown itself

items.when: When data must move to a new tool, to plan field maps, checks and a way back
When the sheet is really several linked tables, to lay them out before any move
When the real need is asking questions of the data, not keeping a bigger workbook

always.when: Before any build, to ask the few questions that settle inputs, outputs and who will use it
When the client has Copilot in Excel and asks what it can do in the workbook itself

helpers.when: When the model is a full budget, forecast or board pack and needs finance judgement
When the numbers come from the books and the ledger itself needs fixing
When the client wants findings from the data, not a sheet that works
When the job spans several apps and should not live in a spreadsheet script
When the sheet has become an app and needs forms, logins and a database
When the question is what the prices should be, not how to calculate a quote

gaps: No library item writes or explains an Excel or Google Sheets formula: lookups, dynamic arrays, LET and LAMBDA
No library item writes, reviews or fixes Excel VBA; the only fits are general code skills
No library item covers Office Scripts or Power Automate for Excel
No library item writes Google Apps Script beyond form replies: timers, custom menus, sidebars and quota limits
No library item builds a quote or price calculator for a trade or service business; only the kit does
No library item covers Power Query or importing and refreshing CSV files
No library item covers locking cells, protected ranges, sharing rights and version history
No library item moves a workbook between Excel and Google Sheets and lists the functions that differ
No library item speeds up a slow workbook: volatile functions, whole-column references and too many links
No library item reviews a Google Sheets file; the review items are written for Excel
No library item lays out different designs of one calculator or tracker to compare
No tool guide covers Excel, Google Sheets or Airtable
